name: bulk_discount
title: Bulk discount on large order lines
body: Wholesale customers buy in bulk. A line of 10 or more units of one item should get 10% off that line. Totals stay in integer cents; round half up.
proposal: Give 10% off any order line of 10 or more units, in line_total, so order_total picks it up.
design: Change `inventory/pricing.py`: `line_total(item, qty)` applies the discount when qty >= 10. Integer arithmetic only: the discounted line is `price_cents * qty * 90 / 100`, rounded half up to a whole cent. `order_total` keeps summing `line_total`.
tasks:
- [ ] In `inventory/pricing.py`, add `BULK_MIN_QTY = 10` and `BULK_DISCOUNT_PCT = 10` module constants.
- [ ] Apply the discount in `line_total` for qty >= BULK_MIN_QTY, rounding half up to the cent with integer arithmetic.
- [ ] Add tests in `tests/test_pricing.py`.
spec:
- 9 units of a 250-cent item cost 2250.
- 10 units of a 250-cent item cost 2250 (2500 less 10%).
- 10 units of a 333-cent item cost 2997.
- 15 units of a 105-cent item cost 1418 (1575 * 0.9 = 1417.5, rounded half up).
- order_total sums the discounted lines.

import unittest

from inventory.models import Item, Order
from inventory.pricing import line_total, order_total
from tests.helpers import store_with


class HiddenBulk(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_lines(self):
        self.assertEqual(line_total(Item("A", "a", 0, 250), 9), 2250)
        self.assertEqual(line_total(Item("A", "a", 0, 250), 10), 2250)
        self.assertEqual(line_total(Item("A", "a", 0, 333), 10), 2997)
        self.assertEqual(line_total(Item("A", "a", 0, 105), 15), 1418)
        self.assertIsInstance(line_total(Item("A", "a", 0, 105), 15), int)

    def test_order(self):
        s = store_with(Item("A", "a", 50, 105), Item("B", "b", 50, 250))
        self.assertEqual(order_total(s, Order("o", [("A", 15), ("B", 2)])), 1918)

name: release_reservation
title: Cancel a reserved order and put its stock back
body: When a customer cancels, the reserved stock should go back on the shelf. Cancelling twice must not add the stock twice.
proposal: Add Store.release(order) that returns a reserved order's stock and marks it cancelled.
design: In `inventory/store.py`, `release(order)`: for an order with status `reserved`, add each line's qty back and set status `cancelled`. Releasing an order already `cancelled` does nothing (no error, no stock change). Releasing a `new` order raises ValueError and changes nothing.
tasks:
- [ ] Add `Store.release(order)` in `inventory/store.py`.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/test_store.py` for release, a second release, and a new order.
spec:
- reserve then release restores every line's qty and sets status `cancelled`.
- a second release is a no-op.
- release of a `new` order raises ValueError.

import unittest

from inventory.models import Item, Order
from tests.helpers import store_with


class HiddenRelease(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_release(self):
        s = store_with(Item("A", "a", 5, 1), Item("B", "b", 4, 1))
        o = Order("o", [("A", 2), ("B", 4)])
        s.reserve(o)
        s.release(o)
        self.assertEqual((s.get("A").qty, s.get("B").qty), (5, 4))
        self.assertEqual(o.status, "cancelled")
        s.release(o)
        self.assertEqual((s.get("A").qty, s.get("B").qty), (5, 4))

    def test_new(self):
        s = store_with(Item("A", "a", 5, 1))
        o = Order("o", [("A", 2)])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            s.release(o)
        self.assertEqual(s.get("A").qty, 5)
        self.assertEqual(o.status, "new")

name: per_item_reorder_level
title: Per-item reorder levels for the low-stock list
body: Fast movers need a higher reorder level than the global threshold. Let an item carry its own level, and list the worst shortfalls first.
proposal: Add an optional reorder level to Item and use it in low_stock, ordered by shortfall.
design: `Item` gets `reorder_level: int | None = None` (last field, so existing positional construction keeps working). `low_stock(store, threshold)`: an item is low when `qty < level`, where level is its `reorder_level` when set, else `threshold`. Order by shortfall (`level - qty`) descending, then SKU ascending. The CLI `low` command keeps working unchanged.
tasks:
- [ ] Add `reorder_level` to `Item` in `inventory/models.py`.
- [ ] Update `low_stock` in `inventory/report.py`.
- [ ] Update `tests/test_report.py`: the existing low-stock and CLI `low` assertions change to the new order.
spec:
- an item with reorder_level 20 and qty 15 is low even when the threshold is 5.
- an item with reorder_level 2 and qty 3 is not low even when the threshold is 5.
- results ordered by shortfall desc, then SKU.

name: cli_value_command
title: CLI: total stock value
body: Finance asks for the value of the stock on hand from the command line.
proposal: Add a `value` command that prints the total value of the stock on hand.
design: In `inventory/cli.py` add a `value` subcommand. Value = sum of `qty * price_cents` over all items (no bulk discount). Print one line: `Stock value: $` followed by dollars with thousands separators and two decimals, e.g. `Stock value: $1,234.56`. Use integer arithmetic for the cents (no float rounding).

- [ ] Tests for both.

from inventory import cli

        return buf.getvalue().strip()

    def test_demo(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli(), "Stock value: $89.97")

    def test_big(self):
        s = store_with(Item("A", "a", 1, 123456789), Item("B", "b", 0, 5))
        self.assertEqual(self.run_cli(s), "Stock value: $1,234,567.89")

name: adjustment_history
title: Keep a history of stock adjustments
body: We can't tell why stock changed. Record each adjustment with a reason.
proposal: Record every successful adjust with its reason, and let callers read a SKU's history.
design: In `inventory/store.py`: `adjust(sku, delta, reason="manual")` appends `(sku, delta, reason)` to the store's history only when it succeeds (a refused adjust records nothing). `history(sku)` returns that SKU's entries as `(delta, reason)` tuples, oldest first; an unknown SKU raises KeyError like `get`. `reserve` is not an adjustment and records nothing.
tasks:
- [ ] Add the history list and the `reason` parameter in `inventory/store.py`.
- [ ] Add `Store.history(sku)`.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/test_store.py`.
spec:
- two adjusts on A then one on B: history("A") is the two A entries in order.
- a refused adjust (would go negative) records nothing.
- history of an unknown SKU raises KeyError.

import unittest

from inventory.models import Item
from tests.helpers import store_with


class HiddenHistory(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_history(self):
        s = store_with(Item("A", "a", 5, 1), Item("B", "b", 5, 1))
        s.adjust("A", 3, "delivery")
        s.adjust("B", -1)
        s.adjust("A", -2)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            s.adjust("A", -100, "oops")
        self.assertEqual(s.history("A"), [(3, "delivery"), (-2, "manual")])
        self.assertEqual(s.history("B"), [(-1, "manual")])
        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
            s.history("Z")

name: find_by_tags
title: Find items by tag
body: The shop front filters by tags. We need a store query that matches all or any of a set of tags.
proposal: Add Store.find(tags, match) for tag filtering.
design: In `inventory/store.py`: `find(tags: list[str], match: str = "all") -> list[Item]`. Tag comparison is case-insensitive. `match="all"`: the item has every requested tag; `match="any"`: at least one. Any other `match` raises ValueError. An empty `tags` list returns every item. Results ordered by SKU.
spec:
- all/any semantics, case-insensitive.
- empty tags returns all items by SKU.
- `match="none"` raises ValueError.

name: csv_import
title: Import stock from a CSV file
body: Suppliers send a CSV of stock levels. Load it into the store: new SKUs are added, known SKUs get the new quantity and price. Bad rows must not stop the import.
proposal: Add report.import_csv(store, text) returning the problems it skipped.
design: In `inventory/report.py`: `import_csv(store, text) -> list[str]`. The text has the header `sku,name,qty,price_cents` (parse with the csv module). For each data row: a new SKU is added as an Item (no tags); a known SKU gets its `name`, `qty` and `price_cents` replaced. A row whose qty or price_cents is not a non-negative integer is skipped and reported as `line N: <reason>` where N is the 1-based line number in the file (the header is line 1). Return the list of reports in file order.
spec:
- adds new items and updates known ones.
- a row with qty `x` on line 3 is reported as starting with `line 3:` and the other rows still import.
- a negative price is skipped and reported.

import unittest

from inventory.models import Item
from inventory.report import import_csv
from tests.helpers import store_with


class HiddenImport(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_import(self):
        s = store_with(Item("A", "old", 1, 100, ["metal"]))
        text = "sku,name,qty,price_cents\nA,Widget,7,150\nB,Bad,x,5\nC,Gizmo,2,999\nD,Neg,1,-5\n"
        problems = import_csv(s, text)
        self.assertEqual(len(problems), 2)
        self.assertTrue(problems[0].startswith("line 3:"), problems)
        self.assertTrue(problems[1].startswith("line 5:"), problems)
        a = s.get("A")
        self.assertEqual((a.name, a.qty, a.price_cents), ("Widget", 7, 150))
        c = s.get("C")
        self.assertEqual((c.name, c.qty, c.price_cents, c.tags), ("Gizmo", 2, 999, []))
        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
            s.get("B")
        with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
            s.get("D")

name: partial_reservation
title: Reserve what we have and backorder the rest
body: Retail orders should ship what is in stock and backorder the rest instead of failing. Also: an order can list the same SKU on more than one line (the shop front does this for bundles), and today reserve() checks each line against the full stock separately, so two lines of 3 against a stock of 4 both pass and the stock goes to -2.
proposal: Add a partial mode to Store.reserve that records backorders, and make every mode count an order's lines for the same SKU together.
design:
In `inventory/models.py`, `Order` gets `backorders: list[tuple[str, int]] = field(default_factory=list)` (needs `field` from dataclasses). In `inventory/store.py`, `reserve(order, allow_partial=False)`:
- Demand per SKU is the sum of that SKU's lines.
- Without `allow_partial`: all or nothing as today, but against the summed demand (two lines of 3 against a stock of 4 is refused, and nothing changes).
- With `allow_partial`: take `min(demand, on hand)` for each SKU; every SKU with a shortfall is appended to `order.backorders` as `(sku, shortfall)`, in the order the SKU first appears in the lines. Status becomes `partial` when there is any backorder, else `reserved`.
- An unknown SKU raises KeyError and changes nothing, in both modes.
tasks:
- [ ] Add `backorders` to `Order` in `inventory/models.py`.
- [ ] Rewrite `Store.reserve` in `inventory/store.py` with summed demand and `allow_partial`.
- [ ] Tests in `tests/test_store.py`.
spec:
- two lines of 3 for a SKU with 4 on hand: refused without allow_partial, stock unchanged, status `new`.
- with allow_partial: stock goes to 0, backorders `[(sku, 2)]`, status `partial`.
- an order fully in stock with allow_partial: status `reserved`, no backorders.
- an unknown SKU raises KeyError and nothing changes.
hidden:
import unittest

from inventory.models import Item, Order
from tests.helpers import store_with


class HiddenPartial(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_duplicate_lines_refused(self):
        s = store_with(Item("A", "a", 4, 1))
        o = Order("o", [("A", 3), ("A", 3)])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            s.reserve(o)
        self.assertEqual((s.get("A").qty, o.status, o.backorders), (4, "new", []))

    def test_partial(self):
        s = store_with(Item("A", "a", 4, 1), Item("B", "b", 10, 1), Item("C", "c", 0, 1))
        o = Order("o", [("C", 2), ("A", 3), ("B", 1), ("A", 3)])
        s.reserve(o, allow_partial=True)
        self.assertEqual((s.get("A").qty, s.get("B").qty, s.get("C").qty), (0, 9, 0))
        self.assertEqual(o.backorders, [("C", 2), ("A", 2)])
        self.assertEqual(o.status, "partial")

    def test_partial_in_stock(self):
        s = store_with(Item("A", "a", 4, 1))
        o = Order("o", [("A", 2), ("A", 2)])
        s.reserve(o, allow_partial=True)
        self.assertEqual((s.get("A").qty, o.status, o.backorders), (0, "reserved", []))

    def test_unknown(self):
        s = store_with(Item("A", "a", 4, 1))
        for partial in (False, True):
            o = Order("o", [("A", 1), ("Z", 1)])
            with self.assertRaises(KeyError):
                s.reserve(o, allow_partial=partial)
            self.assertEqual((s.get("A").qty, o.status), (4, "new"))

name: split_payment
title: Split an order total across several payments
body: Customers can pay with several cards and choose a share for each (for example 50/30/20). The shares must add up to exactly the order total in cents, with no cent lost or invented.
proposal: Add pricing.split_total(total_cents, weights) using the largest-remainder method, and a CLI command to show a split.
design: In `inventory/pricing.py`: `split_total(total_cents: int, weights: list[int]) -> list[int]`. Each part starts as `floor(total * w / sum(weights))`; the cents left over go one each to the parts with the largest fractional remainders (`total * w % sum(weights)`), ties going to the earlier part. Raise ValueError when weights is empty, any weight is negative, all weights are zero, or total is negative. In `inventory/cli.py` add `split TOTAL_CENTS W [W ...]` that prints each part on its own line as dollars with two decimals (`12.34`, no `$`).
tasks:
- [ ] Add `split_total` to `inventory/pricing.py`.
- [ ] Add the `split` command to `inventory/cli.py`.
- [ ] Tests for both.
